article.headline: Zeta Global Jumps 8% After Earnings Call Touts Higher Outlook
article.deck: Zeta closed 0.5% past the 34.90 buy point of a five-week cup, inside a buy range that runs to 36.65.
body: Zeta Global jumped 2.65, or 8.2%, to 35.07 Tuesday, closing above the 34.90 buy point of a five-week cup. The base ran 15.6% deep from its Oct. 5 high to a Nov. 5 low, and the close sits 0.5% over the buy point, inside a buy range that runs to 36.65. Volume was 11,435,430 shares, 1.92x the 50-day average. After hours the stock was at 35.01, down 0.2%, as of 6:16 p.m. Eastern.

The 52-week high is 35.75, 1.9% above the close. Zeta finished 10.3% above its 50-day line at 31.80 and 8.7% above its 21-day line at 32.26. It sits 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line: the session's range still reached the line, so the move is not stretched. The relative strength line hit a new high, and Zeta ranks 99 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 72.3% this year and 79.8% over 12 months.

The quarters table runs through June. June-quarter revenue rose 43.5% from a year earlier to $442.8 million, with EPS of 3 cents. Earnings growth is not available for the quarters given; EPS has moved between a 5-cent loss and a 3-cent profit across the last four. The third-quarter report came Nov. 9. Market value is $8.8 billion at 26.0 times forward earnings.
Tuesday's headlines followed the report. Zacks said the Q3 earnings call highlighted AI growth and a higher outlook, and a GuruFocus headline on the call cited record 46% revenue growth.
A close back under 34.90 would undo the breakout; a run past 36.65 would leave the stock extended.
article.watch: Whether Zeta holds above the 34.90 buy point, with the 52-week high at 35.75 just overhead.

body: ExxonMobil slipped 0.26, or 0.2%, to 164.47 Tuesday on volume 0.84x its 50-day average. body: W.W. Grainger rose 22.98, or 1.6%, to 1,470.65 as of 1:28 p.m. Mountain while all three major indexes traded lower. The stock broke out on Nov. 4 from a 15-week flat base, 12.9% deep, past a 1,420.01 buy point; that session traded 2.39x its 50-day average volume. Four sessions later it sits 3.6% above the buy point, inside a buy range that runs to 1,491.01. Today's volume is on pace for 0.74x average.

The 52-week high of 1,521.41 is 3.3% above. The stock is 1.52 ATRs from the 21-day line, now at 1,384.96, and 11.6% above its 50-day line at 1,318.18, so the trend is intact and not stretched. article.headline: Tempus AI Slips 4.6% After Rally On Data Business, Testing Growth
article.deck: Tempus sits 9.7% below the 89.19 buy point of a six-week cup, a base built below its October 2025 high of 104.32.
body: Tempus AI sells medicine a pipeline of data. The company links a doctor's desktop to its own diagnostic laboratory, runs the results through an analytics platform and keeps them in a repository of patient data that drug researchers can use. Its Hub application lets physicians order and track genetic sequencing tests, and its Lens software serves life sciences companies doing precision research. The tests feed the data business, and the data business sells back into research.

The growth is on the revenue line. September-quarter revenue was $411.5 million, up 23.1% from a year earlier, and sales have climbed in each of the last three quarters in the table, from $348.1 million to $382.5 million to $411.5 million. Earnings have not settled: EPS was an 8-cent loss in the September quarter after a 3-cent profit in June and a 71-cent loss in March. Earnings growth is not available for the quarters given.
The market values Tempus at $14.7 billion. The forward P/E in the payload is negative, so the stock is being priced on its sales and its data, not on profits.

The stock fell 3.90, or 4.6%, to 80.54 Tuesday on volume 0.72x its 50-day average. It is building a six-week cup with an 89.19 buy point and a buy range to 93.65; the cup ran 31.0% deep from a Sept. 29 high to an Oct. 22 low. The close is 9.7% below the buy point. The base formed after a bigger correction: the stock still trades below its Oct. 9, 2025 high of 104.32, and it bottomed at 40.77 on July 28.

The trend under it is sound. Tempus closed 11.7% above its 50-day line at 72.08 and 40.6% above its 200-day line at 57.29, and it sits 0.56 ATRs from the 21-day line at 74.38, not stretched. The relative strength line is 5.9% below its high, and Tempus ranks 97 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 18.5% in a month, 47.5% in three months and 36.4% this year. The 52-week high is 89.09.

The news explains the run. Insider Monkey reported that Tempus surged on data business momentum and an expansion in MRD testing. Zacks said the third-quarter earnings call highlighted growth and 2027 pricing upside, and a Simply Wall St. headline after the Nov. 2 report noted the stock rose 8.7%.
Tuesday's drop came on below-average volume and left the stock above both its 21-day and 50-day lines. The chart work left is the right side of the cup, back up to 89.19.
article.watch: The 21-day line at 74.38 on any further pullback, and the 89.19 buy point above.

chief.verdict: The tape is in correction and the leaders that still work are defensive or one-off: healthcare tops the group table at an average RS of 68 with 88% of its names above the 50-day, while AI infra sits at 20 with 6% and AI chips at 17% above the 50-day. The only fresh, clean breakout is ZETA; the energy names on the story list, OXY and XOM, have already failed their breakouts and cut the 50-day. Risk leans down: the Nasdaq is 5.1% under its 50-day and 9.6% off its high, so most breakouts this week are as likely to retest as to run.
chief.market: With the S&P 500 carrying 7 distribution days (weighted 6.8) and the Nasdaq 6 (weighted 7.8) in a market in correction, keep exposure light, buy only the cleanest pivots in small size and hold cash for the rest.

picks.why: This is the best chart on the desk: a 5-week cup only 15.6% deep, cleared on breakout day at 1.92 times average volume, with the RS line at a new high and RS rank 99. Earnings came out on 2026-11-09 and the stock gained 8.2% the next day, so the report risk is already behind it. The risk is that it is 10.3% above its 50-day in a correcting market, and a cup this short can slip back into the base if the Nasdaq keeps leaking.
picks.entry: Buy from the 34.90 buy point up to 36.65; it closed at 35.07 (0.5% over) and traded 35.01 after hours. Confirmation is a second day holding above 34.90 on above-average volume; a close back under 34.90 means sell it and wait for the next base.

picks.why: A 12-week flat base is the tight, orderly kind of pattern that holds up in a correction, and FAST carries a blue dot for its RS line. RS rank 77 is the weak spot; this is a steady industrial and will not lead a new uptrend by itself.
picks.entry: Buy point 53.02, buy range up to 55.67; at 54.84 (3.4% over) only a small stake is left. Better to add on a pullback toward 53.02 that holds, and cut it on a close back inside the base.

picks.why: The 8-week cup (16.2% deep) is valid and the stock is 4.0% past its 447.13 buy point with RS rank 91 in the strongest group on the desk. But at 465.23 it is nearly at the 469.49 top of the buy range, 9.8% above the 50-day, and the breakout came on only 1.11 times volume, with today's trade at 0.71. Chasing here leaves no room for a normal pullback.
picks.entry: No new buy above 469.49. A pullback to the 21-day line near 449.95, holding above the 447.13 buy point, is the spot to start a position.

picks.why: The 61-week cup is long and sits 0.6% under its 119.88 buy point with RS rank 76, 9.9% above the 50-day. Earnings land on 2026-11-17, within the next five sessions, so a breakout before the report is a coin toss on the number.
picks.entry: Wait for the report. A move through 119.88, up to 125.87, after earnings and on strong volume is the buy; before that, stay out.

avoid.why: The flat-base breakout from 2026-10-23 has failed: it closed at 56.90, 10.9% below the 63.87 buy point and 5.0% under the 50-day, with the RS line 27.5% off its high, so the 1.85 times volume today looks like selling after the report, not support.
The 27-week, 23.5% deep cup broke out on just 1.0 times volume and has fallen back to 164.47, 6.8% below the 176.51 buy point and 2.7% under the 50-day, while oil fell to its lowest since August.

RS rank 95 is the only good thing here: at 225.76 it is 21.4% below the 287.09 buy point and shows up on the sell-signal list as well as the aggressive list, so any early entry means buying a broken 5-week cup in a software group with only 24% of names above the 50-day.
The 6-week cup is 31.0% deep, too loose for this market, and the stock fell 4.6% today to 80.54, still 9.7% under the 89.19 buy point and 11.7% above its 50-day.

chief.watch: Whether ZETA holds above its 34.90 buy point tomorrow while the Nasdaq sits 5.1% under its 50-day; if the one clean breakout on the desk fails, stay in cash.
